c.tagline: Thailand's northernmost major city, home to a dazzling white temple and gateway to the Golden Triangle

taxi.fareNote: Songthaews and tuk-tuks are the standard way around town; Grab is available for longer trips

emergency.note: Tourist police (1155) can assist with English-language support

hood_landmark.City Center / Night Bazaar: Chiang Rai's Night Bazaar and Clock Tower
hood_landmark.Doi Mae Salong: Doi Mae Salong's hilltop tea plantations

hood_desc: The compact downtown with the night bazaar, clock tower, and most hotels and restaurants; the natural base for any visit.
A hilltop Yunnanese Chinese settlement amid tea plantations, offering cooler air and a distinct cultural feel.

The north bank of the Kok River, a couple of kilometres from the clock tower, where riverfront resorts and guesthouses look back at the city across the water. Suits visitors with transport who want gardens, a pool and river views instead of the night bazaar on their doorstep.

water.note: Stick to bottled or filtered water instead of tap.

transit.note: Renting a scooter or car is common for reaching the temples and Golden Triangle independently

air: Mae Fah Luang-Chiang Rai International Airport (CEI)

food.name: Khao soi
food.desc: Northern curry noodle soup in coconut broth with braised chicken, crowned with crisp fried noodles, pickled greens, shallot and lime.

places.note: Michelin-recognised family shop; the khao soi gai is the town benchmark and very cheap.

places.name: Khao Soi Islam

places.name: Khao Soi Vijittra
places.note: Family business that locals have named as the city's best for years.

food.name: Sai ua
food.desc: Coiled Lanna herb sausage of minced pork with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaf and chilli paste, grilled and sliced to eat with sticky rice.

places.name: Kad Luang municipal fresh market

places.name: Phu Lae Restaurant

places.name: Saturday Walking Street

food.name: Nam ngiao noodles
food.desc: Tomato and pork-rib noodle soup coloured with fermented soybean and kapok flowers, topped with blood cubes, a Tai Yai specialty of Chiang Rai.

places.name: Paa Suk Nam Ngiao
places.note: Michelin-listed noodle shop, the address most cited for the dish in Chiang Rai.

places.name: Nam Ngiao Pa Nuan

food.name: Kaeng hang lay
food.desc: Slow-braised pork belly curry with ginger, tamarind, garlic and Burmese-style spice, thick and only mildly hot; eaten with sticky rice.

places.name: Phu Lae Restaurant
places.note: Reliable northern menu in air conditioning; the curry comes with pickled garlic on the side.

places.name: Barrab

places.name: Lung Eed Locol Food

food.name: Larb muang
food.desc: Northern-style minced pork or chicken larb, dry and dark with roasted spice powder rather than lime, served with herbs and crackling.

places.name: Lung Eed Locol Food
places.note: Famous for its crispy chicken larb; a handful of tables and a short menu.

places.name: Barrab
places.note: Cooks the northern version with proper Lanna spice mix, tempered for visitors on request.

places.name: Phu Lae Restaurant
places.note: Easiest introduction to northern larb with English menu and photos.

food.name: Nam prik ong and nam prik noom
food.desc: The two Lanna dips: a tomato-pork chilli relish and a smoky roasted green chilli paste, both scooped up with pork crackling and raw vegetables.

places.name: Barrab

places.name: Phu Lae Restaurant
places.note: Northern set plates include the dips with steamed vegetables and crispy pork.

places.name: Kad Luang municipal fresh market
places.note: Vendors sell the dips by the bag alongside sticky rice for a market breakfast.

food.name: Doi Chaang coffee
food.desc: Arabica grown in the Akha villages of Doi Chang above the city, roasted locally and served hot, iced or as sweet oliang-style brew.

places.name: Doi Chaang Coffee Original
places.note: Flagship cafe of the co-operative that put Chiang Rai coffee on the map.

places.name: Chivit Thamma Da Coffee House
places.note: Colonial-style riverside house, a long-standing favourite for slow coffee and cake.

places.name: Ryokan Cafe
places.note: Small speciality roaster pouring single-origin lots from nearby hill farms.

food.name: Doi Mae Salong oolong tea
food.desc: High-mountain oolong from the Yunnanese settlements north of Chiang Rai, poured gongfu style at the plantations that grow it.

places.name: Choui Fong Tea Plantation
places.note: Hillside tea house and terrace overlooking the rows; day-trip distance from the city.

places.name: Wang Put Tan Tea Plantation
places.note: Working estate with tastings and tea-leaf dishes in its cafe.

places.name: Chiang Rai Night Bazaar
places.note: Stalls sell sealed oolong and jasmine from the same hills to brew or take home.

landmarks: Wat Rong Khun (White Temple)
Artist Chalermchai Kositpipat's surreal all-white temple, encrusted with mirrored mosaic and fantastical sculpture, is contemporary Thailand's most extraordinary and photographed religious artwork.
Baan Dam Museum (Black House)
The brooding counterpoint to the White Temple, artist Thawan Duchanee's compound of forty ebony teak buildings brims with buffalo horns, hides, and dark Lanna art.
Wat Rong Suea Ten (Blue Temple)
A hypnotic sapphire-and-gold temple completed in 2016, its electric-blue interior swirls around a luminous white Buddha in one of Thailand's boldest color statements.
Wat Huay Pla Kang
A 69-meter white Guanyin statue towers over this hillside temple complex, with an elevator to her head for sweeping views across Chiang Rai's valley.
Golden Triangle at Sop Ruak
Where the Mekong and Ruak rivers meet, Thailand, Laos, and Myanmar converge at this storied viewpoint, once heart of the opium trade, now dotted with museums.
Wat Phra Kaew (Chiang Rai)
Thailand's famed Emerald Buddha was discovered here in 1434 inside a lightning-struck chedi; today a jade replica presides over tranquil teak halls.
Chiang Rai Clock Tower
A gilded baroque-Lanna fantasy by the White Temple's creator, this roundabout centerpiece erupts in a nightly light-and-music show at the heart of downtown.
Doi Tung Royal Villa and Mae Fah Luang Garden
The Swiss-Lanna mountain home of the late Princess Mother overlooks spectacular flower terraces, a reforestation triumph atop once-barren opium hills.
Singha Park
A vast agri-tourism estate of rolling tea plantations, flower fields, and lakes just outside town, best explored by bicycle or farm tram.
Khun Korn Waterfall
Chiang Rai province's tallest waterfall plunges seventy meters through lush jungle at the end of a rewarding thirty-minute forest hike.

train.note: Chiang Rai has no railway - the northern line ends at Chiang Mai, about three hours away by road, and the long-planned extension has not been built. State Railway of Thailand services (https://www.dticket.railway.co.th/) run from Chiang Mai to Bangkok overnight. Most visitors arrive by bus or fly into Chiang Rai airport.

intl.to: Bokeo & Luang Prabang (Laos) - via the Chiang Khong / Huay Xai Friendship Bridge
Tachileik (Myanmar) - via the Mae Sai border, status varies
intl.op: local cross-border services — tickets at the Mae Sai crossing

bus.note: Chiang Rai is the gateway to the Golden Triangle borders. Green Bus runs comfortable coaches to Chiang Khong for the Friendship Bridge into Laos, where you cross and pick up Lao transport or the Mekong slow boat to Luang Prabang; Lao visas are available on arrival for most nationalities. The Myanmar crossing at Mae Sai has been closed or restricted at times - check before going. Domestic Green Bus services reach Chiang Mai in about 3 hours and Bangkok overnight in 11-12.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled ferry from Chiang Rai itself. The famous Mekong slow boat to Luang Prabang starts across the border at Huay Xai in Laos, a two-day trip with an overnight stop at Pakbeng, arranged once you have crossed at Chiang Khong. Longtail trips on the Mekong at Sop Ruak in the Golden Triangle are sightseeing rather than transport.

half.name: Mae Salong
half.blurb: A hill village settled by former Kuomintang soldiers, now known for its tea plantations, cherry blossoms and Yunnanese food.

half.name: Chiang Saen
half.blurb: An ancient riverside town on the Mekong with crumbling brick chedis and ruins from a 14th-century Lanna kingdom.

half.name: Mae Sai
half.blurb: Thailand's northernmost town, a bustling border-crossing market facing Tachileik in Myanmar across a small bridge.

full.name: Phu Chi Fa
full.blurb: A dramatic cliffside viewpoint near the Laos border, famous for sunrise seas of fog rolling through the valleys below.

notes.walk: Central Chiang Rai's temples and night bazaar are walkable; the White Temple, Blue Temple, and Golden Triangle require a car, songthaew, or tour
notes.card: Accepted at larger hotels and restaurants; cash preferred at markets
notes.safety: Very safe city, popular with independent travelers. Petty theft is rare; standard travel caution applies near the Golden Triangle border area.
notes.religion: Buddhism (majority); Christianity and animist traditions (notable among hill tribe communities)
notes.langs: Thai; Northern Thai (Lanna dialect); English (moderate in tourist areas)
notes.net: Good 4G coverage in town, patchier in rural hill areas. Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes. ~$5-12 for a 10-15GB prepaid tourist SIM. Free wifi widely available. An AIS or DTAC tourist SIM or eSIM.
notes.transit: Songthaews and tuk-tuks around town; Grab for longer trips
notes.transport: Mae Fah Luang-Chiang Rai International Airport (CEI), about 15 min from downtown. No passenger rail service to Chiang Rai. Long-distance buses connect to Chiang Mai (about 3 hr) and Bangkok (about 11-12 hr). Rental cars and scooters available; well connected via Highway 1 to Chiang Mai.

laundry.pay: coins from changer; Otteri app and QR/PromptPay
